It asks you to turn off your antivirus
Legitimate software almost never asks you to disable your antivirus. This is a classic malware trick.
It mentions a password-protected archive
A password stops antivirus software from scanning what is inside. This is a very common trick for exactly that reason.
It uses words like “crack” or “keygen” that suggest piracy or cheating
Repositories that promise free paid software or game cheats are almost always distributing malware.
It contains an unreadable (encoded) PowerShell command
A command deliberately made unreadable should be assumed to be hiding what it does.
It contains commands that secretly download and run files (mshta, certutil, hidden-window PowerShell)
These commands are typical of scams that ask you to “press Win+R and paste this”. Legitimate software almost never asks you to paste them.
It asks you to “Run as administrator”
With administrator rights it can change anything on your computer. Check whether that is really necessary.
It says antivirus warnings are “false positives”
Sometimes that is true, but it is also a common excuse malware authors use to get you to ignore warnings.

html: GitHub & Hugging Face Check + Safety Scan

Paste a GitHub or Hugging Face (AI model, dataset, or Space) URL and RepoCheck tells you (1) whether it looks safe (signs of malware or impersonation), (2) how to use it, (3) what technology it needs, (4) how hard it is, (5) whether you can use it for work (license), and (6) whether it still works. Setup commands are ready to copy.

Without a token, GitHub allows 60 requests per hour (about 7 checks). With a token, the limit rises to 5,000 per hour.

Mac app: if you have run gh auth login on this Mac, the app uses it automatically (nothing is saved to a file).

Create a token with no permissions at GitHub “Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens” and paste it below. It is stored only in this browser and is never sent to the operator of this site.

How to use this tool

Open the project page on GitHub, copy the address from your browser, and paste it in. The owner/repo form (e.g. openai/whisper) also works, as do Hugging Face model, dataset, and Space URLs. Everything is checked by your browser asking public services (GitHub, Hugging Face, OSV.dev, OpenSSF Scorecard) directly. The URLs you check and the results are never sent to the operator of this site.

What is GitHub? (for non-programmers)

GitHub is where developers around the world publish and share their code. Many powerful free AI tools appear there first. But “click download and it works” is not always true: each repository (one project folder) needs different preparation. This tool explains that preparation in plain language.

Words worth knowing

  • Repository (repo): one project folder. One GitHub page = one repository.
  • README.md: the manual. Always read it first.
  • clone: copy the whole folder to your computer.
  • Releases: the download page for finished builds. If it has a .dmg or .zip, you can install it like any normal app.
  • Issues: the board for bug reports and questions. When you hit an error, search its text here first — someone usually had the same problem.
  • Star: the number of bookmarks. More stars usually means more users and more help available.

Reading licenses (always check before using it for work)

“Free to download” does not mean “free to use for anything”. Common licenses work like this:

LicenseCommercial useNotes
MIT / BSD / ISC / Apache-2.0◎ YesKeep the copyright notice. Apache also requires noting your changes.
MPL-2.0 / LGPL○ YesIf you modify those files, you must publish those modifications.
GPL / AGPL△ With conditionsYou may have to publish the source of your whole program. AGPL applies even if you only run it as a web service.
CC BY-NC and other NC licenses× NoNon-commercial only. Not for paid client work.
No license× Generally noAll rights stay with the author. Ask the author before using it.

* This tool gives a rough guide. For work or anything you publish, read the LICENSE file in the repository yourself. Trained models (weight files) often have a different license from the code, so check those especially carefully.

Common stumbling blocks

  • Wrong Python version: the most common problem is a project that needs 3.10 while you have 3.13. Match the version in the README.
  • Running pip install without a virtual environment: this can break Python for your whole computer. Always install inside a venv.
  • Requires an NVIDIA GPU: it may not run on a Mac, or run extremely slowly. Google Colab is the practical option then.
  • Not updated for a long time: repositories left alone for 2–3 years often break because their libraries changed.
RepoCheck — a safety check for GitHub and Hugging Face (free, no sign-up)

* RepoCheck’s results are a rough guide based on public information. They do not guarantee safety, and some dangers cannot be detected. Download, install, and use anything at your own judgment and risk. The operator is not liable for any damage resulting from use of this tool. License results are also only a guide; for work or anything you publish, always read the LICENSE file itself.
This site shows ads from Google AdSense. Google may use cookies to show them. The URLs you check are not part of the page address, so they are not sent when ads load.
